title: Top K Frequent Elements
followUps: Compare the complexity of sorting all counts, using a size-k heap, and bucket sort. When would you choose each?
How would you compute the top k over a stream of elements that never ends?
How would you compute an approximate top k across logs spread over thousands of machines?
How does your solution behave if k equals the number of distinct elements?

interviewer.approach: Count with a hash map (O(n)). Then either sort by count O(u log u), keep a min-heap of size k O(u log k), or bucket sort by frequency O(n). Bucket sort is the optimal answer; a heap is a strong answer. Quickselect is O(u) average.
hints: Start by figuring out how often each element appears. What structure makes that easy?
Once you have counts, do you need to fully sort them to get the top k? What structure keeps only the k best?
Frequencies are bounded by n. Could you index buckets by frequency instead of sorting?
pitfalls: Using a max-heap over all elements (O(u log u)) and claiming O(n log k).
Off-by-one in bucket sizes (frequency can equal n).

dimensions.name: Questioning the AI's complexity claims
dimensions.signals: Checked the complexity the AI stated rather than repeating it: a heap of size k is O(n log k), sorting all counts is O(n log n), bucket sort is O(n). Picked the approach that meets the requirement and could explain why; verified the result returns elements, not counts.

levels.1: Repeated an incorrect AI complexity claim, or couldn't say what the code costs.
levels.2: Roughly right on complexity but didn't examine the AI's claim or the alternatives.
levels.3: Stated the correct complexity of the adopted approach and compared it with one alternative.
levels.4: Caught an overstated AI claim, or steered the AI to the better approach, with a precise analysis.

watchFor: Claiming O(n) for a heap-based solution, or O(n log k) for one that sorts every count.
Bucket-sort off-by-one: a frequency can be as large as n, so n + 1 buckets are needed.
Returning the counts, or (element, count) pairs, instead of the elements.
Pushing every element into an unbounded heap and popping k times: O(n log n), not O(n log k).
